name: Security Alert and Event Evaluation Record
description: The population of security alerts raised during the period and the recorded outcome of analysing each: who assessed it, when, and whether it was judged to be a security event or incident.

expected_content.element: Unfiltered alert population for the examination period
expected_content.why: A filtered export hides the unanalysed backlog, which is the substance of the control.

expected_content.element: Alert timestamp, source, and affected component
expected_content.why: Places the alert in the period and connects it to the in-scope boundary.
Demonstrates a defined responder acted, which is what distinguishes monitoring from collection.

expected_content.element: Disposition with its basis: benign, security event, or declared incident
expected_content.why: The discriminating judgement CC7.2 and CC7.3 both rest on.

expected_content.element: Link to the incident record where the event was declared an incident
expected_content.why: Connects the evaluation to the response, so the chain is traceable end to end.

expected_content.element: Elapsed time from alert to analysis measured against the entity's committed timeframe
expected_content.why: Timeliness is assessed against the entity's own commitment, which is the only benchmark.

source_system_examples: SIEM case or alert queue export

freshness_expectation.rationale: DriftGuard default: the record must reach the end of the period under assessment.

redaction_guidance: Alert detail can describe live weaknesses; restrict distribution.
Retain analyst identity for attribution; affected user identities may be tokenised.
retention_guidance: Retain for the full examination period; shorter retention leaves an interval where analysis cannot be demonstrated.

validation_rules.rule: An alert population export exists covering the examination period.
The export is unfiltered rather than limited to closed or escalated items.
Each alert carries an analyst, a disposition, and the basis for that disposition.
Analysis occurred within the entity's committed timeframe for the alert severity.
Alerts judged to be incidents link to a corresponding incident record.
The export originates from the alerting or ticketing platform rather than a summary narrative.

common_issues.issue: Only escalated alerts exported, so the unanalysed remainder is invisible.
common_issues.impact: The population is incomplete and analysis coverage cannot be assessed.

common_issues.issue: Alerts auto-closed by rule with no recorded basis.
common_issues.impact: Informed suppression cannot be distinguished from alerts nobody examined.

common_issues.issue: Dispositions recorded with no criteria stating what makes an alert an incident.

source_refs.supports: Expected content, persuasiveness weighting, and the common issues list.
Freshness window, sensitivity classification, and redaction guidance.

notes: Distinct from EV-ENDPOINT-002, which is the malware-specific detection population feeding this process. This record is the consolidated alert and event evaluation layer; do not duplicate one into the other.
